description: Delivering a project after the money is awarded: agreement, authorization, procurement, progress reporting, reimbursement and closeout — the administrative spine every grant carries.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the award date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.

Offsets run from the award date because that is the date every grant obligation is counted from. Your agreement's own milestone dates override every offset here — enter them as soon as the agreement is executed.
It is deliberately administrative. The technical work the grant pays for is a separate work plan applied alongside this one.
Reimbursement timing, allowable costs and records retention are set by the agreement and by whoever audits it. None of them are stated here.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.

deliverables.title: Executed agreement package and project file
deliverables.summary: The signed agreement, its exhibits, the approved scope and schedule, filed where the whole team can find them.

deliverables.title: Delivery schedule with funder milestone dates
deliverables.summary: The project schedule with every date the agreement requires entered as a real deadline.

deliverables.title: Procurement package
deliverables.summary: The solicitation for the consultant or contractor services the project needs, prepared to the standard the agreement requires.

deliverables.title: First progress report
deliverables.summary: The first report in the format and cadence the agreement sets.

deliverables.title: First reimbursement request package
deliverables.summary: The first invoice with its supporting documentation, assembled the way every later one will be.

deliverables.title: Monitoring and records file
deliverables.summary: The documentation an auditor would ask for, assembled as the work happens rather than at closeout.

deliverables.title: Closeout package
deliverables.summary: Final report, final invoice, and the records retained for the period the agreement requires.

milestones.title: Award accepted and agreement executed
milestones.summary: The agreement is signed by both parties.

milestones.title: Funding authorization confirmed in writing
milestones.summary: Written confirmation that costs may be incurred — the step that most often gets skipped and most often costs money.

milestones.title: Consultant or contractor contract awarded
milestones.summary: The delivery team is under contract.

milestones.title: Midpoint progress review with the funder
milestones.summary: Scope, schedule and spend reviewed while there is still time to change them.

milestones.title: Final invoice submitted
milestones.summary: The last reimbursement request goes in.

milestones.title: Closeout accepted by the funder
milestones.summary: The funder confirms the project is complete and the file may close.
